arXiv:2609.13268v1 [cs.CV] 07 Sep 2026

Capability-Routed Visual Retrieval and Evidence Threading for Long-Context Document Question Answering

Amirul Rahman    Aisha Karim    Kenji Nakamura    Yi-Fan Ng Affiliation: University of Malaya Email: kenjinakamura@um.edu.my
Abstract

Annual reports, diligence packs, and infographic dashboards bury numbers in page images: axes, cell grids, and footnotes that OCR pipelines flatten and that page-level visual retrievers still treat as interchangeable in-context examples. We keep a frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct generator and a ColPali / VisRAG-Ret page index, and insert three modules. A capability-aware visual router (CAVR) tags each retrieved page as text, table, chart, layout, or mixed and mixes specialist experts before generation. Weak-to-strong page selection (WSPS) distils a frozen 7B answerability teacher into a 3B selection head so ranking is no longer a single InfoNCE score. Visual evidence threading (VET) builds layout-anchored paths of length at most three and lets the generator read the thread rather than a flat top-kk list. On gold-page DocVQA / ChartQA / InfographicVQA the 7B system reaches 96.3 / 90.1 / 85.4. Under the VisRAG top-3 protocol the mean generation accuracy is 62.74 versus 59.39 for the same backbone with concatenation. On MMLongBench-Doc retrieve-then-read, F1 moves from 19.2 to 22.6 and multi-page accuracy from 16.4 to 21.2. ViDoRe nDCG@5 after WSPS reranking is 83.6, with TAT-DQA financial reports at 70.4.

1 Introduction

Financial filings and business PDFs are not natural photographs. A query about operating margin may need a line chart on one page, a consolidated table two pages later, and a polarity-reversing footnote in the notes. Text retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) first runs optical character recognition (OCR) and then embeds chunks Lewis et al. (2020); Karpukhin et al. (2020); Robertson and Zaragoza (2009). Layout, axis ticks, and cell alignment die in that parse. Vision-first retrievers such as ColPali and VisRAG keep the page as an image Faysse et al. (2025); Yu et al. (2025), which is the right unit for annual reports, yet the generator still concatenates the top-kk pages as if they were homogeneous visual prompts.

Zhou et al. (2024) showed that a handful of visual in-context examples can steer a large vision–language model (VLM). That result assumes the examples share a skill and that order is secondary. Adjacent pages in a 10-K do not: one is a bar chart, one is a dense legal opinion, one is a split balance sheet. Concatenating them is closer to stuffing a chaotic context than to visual in-context learning. On VisRAG, MiniCPM-V 2.0 ChartQA accuracy falls from 34.92 at top-1 to 22.22 at top-3 page concatenation Yu et al. (2025); Yao et al. (2024b), so “more pages as more shots” is already false. MMLongBench-Doc further shows that even GPT-4o scores only 44.9 F1 when it reads whole PDFs of 47.5 pages on average, and open LVLMs that concatenate every page often trail OCR-then-LLM stacks Ma et al. (2024); OpenAI (2024).

Three structural gaps remain after 2025 visual document RAG. Retrievers score semantic near-neighbours; they do not say whether a page should be read by an OCR expert, a table merger, or a chart-axis head Hu et al. (2024); Masry et al. (2022). A 3B late-interaction index and a 7B reader are not the same model, so contrastive ranks can hide the page that the reader could actually use. Cross-page evidence is a visual stream of running headers, cropped tables, and captions that live on a different folio than the figure—a setting that layout-aware graphs and agentic planners attack with heavier controllers Sourati et al. (2026); Zuo et al. (2026b); Yang et al. (2026), not with a short, layout-anchored thread that a frozen 7B decoder can consume.

We freeze Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct Bai et al. (2025) and a ColPali or VisRAG-Ret index, and insert three modules (Figure 1 and Section 3): capability-aware visual routing (CAVR), weak-to-strong page selection (WSPS), and visual evidence threading (VET). Contributions:

  • •

    CAVR classifies each retrieved page into text, table, chart, layout, or mixed skill and mixes four light experts so heterogeneous pages are no longer one visual channel.

  • •

    WSPS trains a selection head on frozen 7B answerability labels, then interpolates that head with late-interaction retrieval.

  • •

    VET compiles layout anchors into directed paths of length L≤3L{\leq}3 and serialises the winning path. Ours (CAVR+WSPS+VET) reaches 96.3 / 90.1 / 85.4 on gold-page DocVQA / ChartQA / InfoVQA, 62.74 mean VisRAG-protocol accuracy, 22.6 MMLongBench-Doc F1, and 83.6 ViDoRe nDCG@5.

2 Related Work

2.1 Document VLMs and visual in-context learning

OCR-free readers—Donut, Pix2Struct, UReader, Monkey, CogAgent, DocOwl 1.5—treat a page as a screenshot and emit answers or structured markup Kim et al. (2022); Lee et al. (2023); Ye et al. (2023); Liu et al. (2024); Hong et al. (2024); Hu et al. (2024). General VLMs (Qwen-VL, Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL, LLaVA-OneVision, PaliGemma, MiniCPM-V) raise DocVQA into the mid-90s at 7B–72B Bai et al. (2023); Wang et al. (2024); Bai et al. (2025); Chen et al. (2024b); Chen et al. (2024a); Li et al. (2024); Beyer et al. (2024); Yao et al. (2024b). Chart pretraining such as MatCha derenders plots into math Liu et al. (2023); knowledge-augmented VL transformers inject text facts beside pixels Gui et al. (2022). Modular VQA compiles a question into a program over specialists Subramanian et al. (2023), which is the right shape for heterogeneous pages, but those programs assume cropped natural images, not retrieved PDF folios. Visual ICL concatenates labelled images; Zhou et al. (2025) show that weak-to-strong generalisation fails when one teacher signal mixes many capabilities. We take that multi-capability diagnosis into visual RAG: chart reading, table alignment, and layout localisation are not one skill, so they should not share one projection.

2.2 Visual document RAG and late interaction

Text RAG for knowledge-intensive QA is mature Lewis et al. (2020); Zhang et al. (2023); Saad-Falcon et al. (2024). Visual RAG attaches an image to the query Lin and Byrne (2022); Ramos et al. (2023); Chen et al. (2023); medical rationale-guided RAG insists that answers cite retrieved evidence Sohn et al. (2025). Multilingual RAG in 2026 is still largely textual Ranaldi et al. (2026). On documents, ColBERT-style late interaction Khattab and Zaharia (2020) moved to page patches in ColPali Faysse et al. (2025); Beyer et al. (2024) and to whole-page VisRAG-Ret Yu et al. (2025). SigLIP, BiPali, and OCR+BGE pipelines are the standard ViDoRe baselines Zhai et al. (2023); Xiao et al. (2023); Lee et al. (2024). 2026 systems scale the same late-interaction idea: Nemotron ColEmbed V2 tops ViDoRe V3 de Souza P. Moreira et al. (2026); AnchorFold and ColSNAP compress patch indexes Zuo et al. (2026a); Singha Roy et al. (2026); PULSAR pools ColPali-style vectors for enterprise decks Constable et al. (2026). MARA reweights regions by the query Wu et al. (2025); LAD-RAG adds a symbolic layout graph and an agent Sourati et al. (2026); MAGE-RAG builds a page–element graph and a budgeted controller Zuo et al. (2026b); MM-R2 plans what and where before search Yang et al. (2026). Those stacks either enlarge the retriever or wrap an LLM agent around it. We keep the 3B index and change how pages are routed, selected, and threaded for a 7B reader.

Long-context alignment further shows that not every token in a long window is equally useful: GATEAU selects influential samples before alignment Si et al. (2025). Page selection is the visual analogue—a retrieved folio can be topically close and still unusable for answering.

2.3 Long PDFs, threads, and faithfulness

DocVQA, ChartQA, InfographicVQA, and MMLongBench-Doc define the evaluation surface we use Mathew et al. (2021); Masry et al. (2022); Mathew et al. (2022); Ma et al. (2024). Cross-page items are 33.7% of MMLongBench-Doc; financial reports are 8.1% of its documents. Concatenating every page, or packing five pages into one canvas, cuts the thread. We want a short directed path with layout anchors, not a free-form agent trace and not a second copy of visual ICL. CLIP-style dual encoders remain a useful single-vector reference Radford et al. (2021) but lose the patch matches ColPali keeps.

3 Method

A text query qq and a corpus 𝒫\mathcal{P} of page images map to an answer yy. Figure 1 shows the flow. Retrieval is frozen ColPali or VisRAG-Ret; generation is Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with LoRA Hu et al. (2022); Bai et al. (2025). CAVR, WSPS, and VET are the only trained modules.

3.1 Problem formulation

Let 𝒟K⊂𝒫\mathcal{D}_{K}\subset\mathcal{P} be the top-KK pages under late interaction (K=20K{=}20). CAVR emits page representations {hi}\{h_{i}\}, WSPS keeps a subset 𝒟k\mathcal{D}_{k} with k=3k{=}3, and VET returns a thread TT. Decoding is

p⁡(y∣q,𝒫)=Decϕ​(q,T⁡(q,𝒟k)).\displaystyle p(y\mid q,\mathcal{P})=\mathrm{Dec}_{\phi}\bigl(q,\,T(q,\mathcal{D}_{k})\bigr). (1)

The decoder in (1) never sees the raw top-kk list. Oracle pages, when used in analysis, replace 𝒟k\mathcal{D}_{k} but still pass CAVR and VET.

3.2 Retriever

ColPali encodes qq as token vectors {qt}\{q_{t}\} and a page PP as patch vectors {pj}\{p_{j}\}. Late-interaction MaxSim Khattab and Zaharia (2020); Faysse et al. (2025) is

sret​(q,P)=∑tmaxj⁡⟨qt,pj⟩.\displaystyle s_{\mathrm{ret}}(q,P)=\sum_{t}\max_{j}\langle q_{t},p_{j}\rangle. (2)

VisRAG-Ret substitutes a pooled page vector for {pj}\{p_{j}\} on the VisRAG protocol Yu et al. (2025). We do not fine-tune (2); WSPS only reranks.

3.3 CAVR: capability-aware visual router

Visual ICL assumes homogeneous shots. Document pages do not. A five-way linear head on the ColPali patch mean predicts a skill

ri=softmax⁡(Wr​p¯i+br)∈Δ4,\displaystyle r_{i}=\mathrm{softmax}(W_{r}\,\bar{p}_{i}+b_{r})\in\Delta^{4}, (3)

with classes {text,table,chart,layout,mixed}\{\mathrm{text},\mathrm{table},\mathrm{chart},\mathrm{layout},\mathrm{mixed}\} in (3). Supervision comes from dataset metadata (ChartQA→\tochart, TAT-DQA / WikiTableQuestions→\totable, dense DocVQA pages→\totext, InfographicVQA→\tomixed) and DocOwl-style structure tags Hu et al. (2024). Four experts then read PiP_{i}: EtextE_{\mathrm{text}} is the Qwen2.5-VL dynamic-resolution ViT; EtableE_{\mathrm{table}} merges horizontal neighbour patches; EchartE_{\mathrm{chart}} concatenates axis-tick OCR; ElayoutE_{\mathrm{layout}} keeps region bounding tokens. A query-conditioned gate

gi=softmax⁡(Wg​[ri;q])\displaystyle g_{i}=\mathrm{softmax}\bigl(W_{g}[r_{i};q]\bigr) (4)

mixes experts in (5):

hi=∑egi,e​Ee​(Pi).\displaystyle h_{i}=\sum_{e}g_{i,e}\,E_{e}(P_{i}). (5)

The generator prompt prefixes the argmax skill from (4). Ablating CAVR forces every page through EtextE_{\mathrm{text}}. Mixing experts is cheaper than a sparse mixture-of-experts language model Jiang et al. (2024): the gate is a 5×45{\times}4 matrix on a 7B reader, not a 8×\times22B decoder.

3.4 WSPS: weak-to-strong page selection

A single InfoNCE rank cannot lift chart reading and clause localisation together Zhou et al. (2025). We freeze the 7B generator and, for each candidate PiP_{i} in 𝒟K\mathcal{D}_{K}, record whether the gold answer is extractable from (q,Pi)(q,P_{i}) under relaxed match (ChartQA-style ±5%\pm 5\% on numbers Masry et al. (2022)). Gold evidence pages are positives. The teacher probability and hard label are

πi=pϕ(span(y)∣q,Pi),yi=𝟏[πi≥τ]∨𝟏[Pi∈𝒫⋆],\displaystyle\pi_{i}=p_{\phi}(\mathrm{span}(y)\mid q,P_{i}),\qquad y_{i}=\mathbf{1}[\pi_{i}\geq\tau]\lor\mathbf{1}[P_{i}\in\mathcal{P}^{\star}], (6)

with τ=0.35\tau{=}0.35 in (6). A linear head ssel​(q,Pi)s_{\mathrm{sel}}(q,P_{i}) on the retriever’s late-interaction summary is trained with

ℒWSPS=BCE(ssel,y)+βKL(ssel∥π),β=0.3.\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{WSPS}}=\mathrm{BCE}(s_{\mathrm{sel}},y)+\beta\,\mathrm{KL}(s_{\mathrm{sel}}\|\pi),\qquad\beta=0.3. (7)

The 7B weights are not updated in (7). Test-time fusion is

s⁡(q,Pi)=λret​sret+λsel​ssel​(q,Pi),\displaystyle s(q,P_{i})=\lambda_{\mathrm{ret}}s_{\mathrm{ret}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{sel}}s_{\mathrm{sel}}(q,P_{i}), (8)

with default λsel=0.4\lambda_{\mathrm{sel}}{=}0.4 in (8) and λret=1−λsel\lambda_{\mathrm{ret}}{=}1-\lambda_{\mathrm{sel}}. Per-skill temperatures τe\tau_{e} on ssels_{\mathrm{sel}} stop dense-text pages from crowding out charts:

s~sel=τe⁡(i)−1​ssel​(q,Pi).\displaystyle\tilde{s}_{\mathrm{sel}}=\tau_{e(i)}^{-1}s_{\mathrm{sel}}(q,P_{i}). (9)

(9) is a calibration, not a second retriever. Contextual faithfulness training that rewrites the generator Si et al. (2026a) is complementary: we change which pages enter the window, not the RL objective.

3.5 VET: visual evidence threading

Zhou et al. (2023) insert a “first summarise, then reason” step in chaotic text. Multi-page PDFs are chaotic because headers repeat, tables split across folios, and captions drift from figures. We build a directed graph whose nodes are pages plus layout anchors (title block, header row, legend, page number) as in (10),

vi=(Pi,ai,ri),ai=Anchor⁡(Pi).\displaystyle v_{i}=(P_{i},a_{i},r_{i}),\qquad a_{i}=\mathrm{Anchor}(P_{i}). (10)

Edge weights in (11) mix folio adjacency, numeric coreference, entity overlap, and skill complementarity (chart then table, never two redundant OCR pages):

wi​j=αadj𝟏[|ni−nj|=1]+αnumcoref(ai,aj)+αentJaccard(ai,aj)+αskcomp(ri,rj).\displaystyle w_{ij}=\alpha_{\mathrm{adj}}\mathbf{1}[|n_{i}-n_{j}|{=}1]+\alpha_{\mathrm{num}}\mathrm{coref}(a_{i},a_{j})+\alpha_{\mathrm{ent}}\mathrm{Jaccard}(a_{i},a_{j})+\alpha_{\mathrm{sk}}\mathrm{comp}(r_{i},r_{j}). (11)

Nodes that contradict a query slot (opposite polarity, disjoint numeric interval) are dropped by (12),

V′={v∈V:compat⁡(q,v)=1},\displaystyle V^{\prime}=\{v\in V:\mathrm{compat}(q,v)=1\}, (12)

and we keep directed paths of length at most LL from the highest WSPS node:

T⋆=argmaxT:|T|≤L∑(vi,vj)∈Twi​j,L=3.\displaystyle T^{\star}=\arg\max_{T:|T|\leq L}\sum_{(v_{i},v_{j})\in T}w_{ij},\qquad L=3. (13)

Up to three paths from (13) are serialised as interleaved image–anchor–skill tokens

seq⁡(T)=[Pi​∣ai∣​ri]i∈T.\displaystyle\mathrm{seq}(T)=\bigl[P_{i}\mid a_{i}\mid r_{i}\bigr]_{i\in T}. (14)

The decoder reads (14), not 𝒟k\mathcal{D}_{k}:

y=Decϕ​(q,seq⁡(T⋆)).\displaystyle y=\mathrm{Dec}_{\phi}\bigl(q,\,\mathrm{seq}(T^{\star})\bigr). (15)

Teacher threads come from MMLongBench-Doc evidence-page labels Ma et al. (2024). At test time we rank paths by slot satisfaction and generation confidence. VET is a three-hop graph over pages, not an agent loop.

3.6 Training

Stage 1 freezes the ViT and trains the CAVR skill head and gate for two epochs (page classification plus routing consistency). Stage 2 freezes the generator and trains WSPS for two epochs. Stage 3 jointly trains VET edge prediction and answer LoRA for three epochs. The sum in (16) is

ℒ=ℒCAVR+ℒWSPS+ℒVET+ℒCE.\displaystyle\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CAVR}}+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{WSPS}}+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{VET}}+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CE}}. (16)

Inference uses greedy decoding on (15). Complexity of VET scoring is linear in kk plus O⁡(|V′|2)O(|V^{\prime}|^{2}) compatibility, with k≤8k{\leq}8.

4 Experimental Setup

4.1 Datasets and protocols

DocVQA has 12,767 page images and 50,000 questions from 6,071 UCSF industrial files; we report ANLS and accuracy Mathew et al. (2021). ChartQA mixes 9.6k human and 23.1k generated questions over Statista / Pew style plots; the metric is relaxed accuracy with a 5% numeric tolerance Masry et al. (2022). InfographicVQA has 5,485 infographics and 30,035 questions Mathew et al. (2022). MMLongBench-Doc holds 135 PDFs (mean 47.5 pages) and 1,082 questions split into single-page (SIN), multi-page (MUL), and unanswerable (UNA) Ma et al. (2024). VisRAG-protocol numbers use a shared VisRAG-Ret index and top-3 visual generation on ArxivQA, ChartQA, DocVQA, InfoVQA, PlotQA, and SlideVQA Yu et al. (2025). ViDoRe reports nDCG@5, including TAT-DQA financial reports Faysse et al. (2025). Main comparisons are open models at ≤10{\leq}10B. Closed APIs, OCR+LLM cascades, full-PDF concatenation, and Oracle pages are reference rows.

4.2 Implementation

The generator is Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct Bai et al. (2025). Retrieval is ColPali (PaliGemma backbone) except on the VisRAG protocol, which uses VisRAG-Ret Faysse et al. (2025); Yu et al. (2025); Beyer et al. (2024). LoRA rank r=16r{=}16, α=32\alpha{=}32 on attention projections. K=20K{=}20, k=3k{=}3, λsel=0.4\lambda_{\mathrm{sel}}{=}0.4, L=3L{=}3. Batch size 4 on A100-80GB, AdamW, peak learning rate 1×10−41{\times}10^{-4} for adapters and 2×10−52{\times}10^{-5} for LoRA. Ours is always named Ours (CAVR+WSPS+VET).

5 Results

5.1 Gold-page document VQA

Table 1 is the ≤10{\leq}10B open comparison on gold pages. Qwen2.5-VL-7B already sits at 95.7 / 87.3 / 82.6 on DocVQA / ChartQA / InfoVQA Bai et al. (2025). Ours moves those columns to 96.3 / 90.1 / 85.4. The ChartQA lift (+2.8+2.8) is larger than DocVQA (+0.6+0.6), which matches CAVR: WSPS barely changes recall when the gold page is given, so the expert mix is doing the work. DocOwl 1.5 remains the strongest 8B OCR-free specialist at 81.6 / 70.5 / 50.4 Hu et al. (2024); UReader, Qwen-VL, and Monkey trail as in the DocOwl table Ye et al. (2023); Bai et al. (2023); Liu et al. (2024). CogAgent (17.3B) and InternVL2.5-78B / Qwen2.5-VL-72B are scale references, not the winning set Hong et al. (2024); Chen et al. (2024a); Bai et al. (2025). Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o are closed Anthropic (2024); OpenAI (2024). Table 2 copies the DocOwl 1.5 OCR-free DocVQA column so the older Donut / Pix2Struct / DocOwl numbers stay attached to their source Kim et al. (2022); Lee et al. (2023); Hu et al. (2024). Dataset-paper BERT extractors in Table 3 top out at 0.665 test ANLS Mathew et al. (2021); they are a historical floor, not competitors.

5.2 ChartQA and InfographicVQA dataset floors

Table 4 restates the ChartQA paper’s overall ranking: VL-T5 pretrained at 51.84 is the original ceiling Masry et al. (2022). Table 5 restates InfographicVQA: LayoutLM in-domain at 0.272 test ANLS, humans at 0.980 Mathew et al. (2022). Modern OCR-free ChartQA / InfoVQA columns of DocOwl 1.5 (Pix2Struct 58.6 / 40.0, DocOwl 57.4 / 38.2, CogAgent 68.4 / 44.5, DocOwl-1.5 70.5 / 50.4) sit between those floors and Table 1. Ours does not compete against VL-T5; it competes against Qwen2.5-VL-7B on the same gold page.

5.3 VisRAG open retrieval

Table 6 uses one VisRAG-Ret index and top-3 visual generation Yu et al. (2025). MiniCPM-V 2.6 averages 56.12; swapping the generator to Qwen2.5-VL-7B concatenation reaches 59.39. Ours averages 62.74 (+3.35+3.35, +5.6%+5.6\% relative) without crossing the MiniCPM-V 2.6 Oracle at 67.78. ChartQA (57.97→62.0857.97\to 62.08) and PlotQA (45.58→52.4245.58\to 52.42) move more than ArxivQA, which is the CAVR claim. DocVQA (74.36→77.9274.36\to 77.92) closes about one third of the MiniCPM Oracle gap on that column (83.25−70.9083.25-70.90), matching the WSPS story that many errors are wrong pages rather than unread gold pages. SlideVQA, a multi-page deck task, rises 52.68→54.7052.68\to 54.70 (+2.02+2.02), the VET column. LLaVA-OneVision-7B, InternVL2-8B, and Qwen2-VL-7B fill the open visual-generator ladder Li et al. (2024); Chen et al. (2024b); Wang et al. (2024). OCR generators (MiniCPM OCR 26.71, GPT-4o OCR 45.91) and GPT-4o vision top-3 (54.98) are references. In-domain MRR@10 after WSPS reranking is 80.42, versus 77.91 VisRAG-Ret, 76.54 ColPali, and 74.78 MiniCPM OCR Yu et al. (2025).

5.4 MMLongBench-Doc retrieve-then-read

Table 7 recalls k=3k{=}3 pages with the listed retriever and reads them with the listed generator. ColPali + Qwen2.5-VL-7B concatenation is the strongest open retrieve-then-read baseline (ACC 20.8, F1 19.2). Ours reaches 24.1 / 22.6 (+3.4+3.4 F1). SigLIP and BiPali under the same 7B reader show that a weaker first stage still hurts Zhai et al. (2023); Faysse et al. (2025). MiniCPM-V 2.6 and InternVL2-8B as readers sit below the Qwen2.5 concatenation line Yao et al. (2024b); Chen et al. (2024b). Full-PDF concatenation (InternVL-Chat-v1.5 F1 13.0, InternLM-XComposer2 F1 9.8) is a different protocol Chen et al. (2024b); Dong et al. (2024). Mixtral-Instruct OCR+LLM (F1 24.7) and GPT-4o whole-PDF (F1 44.9) are cascades or closed systems Jiang et al. (2024); OpenAI (2024); humans score 66.0 F1 Ma et al. (2024). Table 8 splits evidence type: MUL (cross-page) moves 16.4→21.216.4\to 21.2 (+4.8+4.8), larger than SIN (+3.2+3.2), which is the VET claim. Chart (CHA) and table (TAB) evidence also rise, consistent with CAVR experts. Long-horizon agent planners Si et al. (2026b) would spend extra tool steps on the same PDFs; we stay inside a three-page thread.

5.5 ViDoRe retrieval

Table 9 reranks ColPali’s top-20 with WSPS and reports nDCG@5 Faysse et al. (2025). ColPali averages 81.3; Ours averages 83.6. TATQ (TAT-DQA financial reports) moves 65.8→70.465.8\to 70.4 (+4.6+4.6), the largest single-column gain, which is the intended business-document offset. OCR BM25 and BGE-M3 remain far below vision-first indexes Robertson and Zaragoza (2009); Xiao et al. (2023). SigLIP / BiSigLIP / BiPali confirm that single-vector or pooled VLMs underperform late interaction Zhai et al. (2023). We do not claim to beat Nemotron ColEmbed V2 on ViDoRe V3 de Souza P. Moreira et al. (2026); that is a different, larger embedding family. AnchorFold and ColSNAP compress indexes rather than rerank for answerability Zuo et al. (2026a); Singha Roy et al. (2026).

6 Analysis

6.1 Ablations

Table 10 freezes Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct + ColPali recall. Concatenation of top-3 pages is 59.39 / 19.2 / 87.3 on VisRAG average / MMLong F1 / gold ChartQA. Each module helps; CAVR is strongest on ChartQA (89.189.1), WSPS on VisRAG average (61.0861.08), VET on MMLong F1 (20.620.6). Pairing CAVR with WSPS already reaches 61.88 / 21.5 / 89.6, and the full model matches the main tables (62.74 / 22.6 / 90.1). Routing every page through EtextE_{\mathrm{text}}, dropping teacher answerability, or flattening VET to an unordered top-kk all fall back near the concatenation floor, so the sub-mechanisms are not decorative.

6.2 Hyper-parameters

Figure 2(a) in Figure 2 and Table 11 vary the page budget kk. VisRAG average and MMLong F1 peak at the default k=3k{=}3 (62.74 / 22.6). k=1k{=}1 under-recalls (57.12 / 17.8); k=8k{=}8 reintroduces noise (61.20 / 21.1). Table 12 scans λsel\lambda_{\mathrm{sel}} in (8): 0.00.0 is CAVR+WSPS with the selection head off (61.88 / 21.5), 0.40.4 is the default, and 0.80.8 overfits the teacher (61.96 / 21.8). Table 13 varies VET depth: L=1L{=}1 is a single-page thread (MUL 18.6); L=3L{=}3 is best (MUL 21.2); L=5L{=}5 adds conflicting hops (20.1). Defaults sit at the peak, not on a monotone ramp. DeepSeek-VL and Idefics2 are not in the winning set; we mention them only as additional open VLMs that could host the same three modules Lu et al. (2024); Laurençon et al. (2024). Gemini 1.5 remains a long-context closed reference Gemini Team (2024).

6.3 Document types

Figure 2(b) and Table 14 split MMLongBench-Doc F1 by document type Ma et al. (2024). Industry files are already formatted; the gain is +2.6+2.6. Academic papers sit in between (+3.7+3.7). Infographic-heavy research reports (+4.8+4.8) and financial reports (+5.6+5.6) move more, which is the intended vertical: tables plus notes that span folios. PULSAR’s production decks are the same visual regime Constable et al. (2026); we evaluate public benchmarks rather than a private deal room.

6.4 Efficiency

Figure 3(b) in Figure 3 and Table 15 report page encoding on an L4 (ColPali protocol) and end-to-end QA latency for k=3k{=}3 on one A100-80GB Faysse et al. (2025). Full Ours encodes a page in 0.46 s versus 0.39 s for ColPali and answers in 2.84 s versus 2.51 s concatenation (+0.33+0.33 s) with +41+41M trainable parameters. VisRAG average rises 59.39→\to62.74. Unstructured OCR+caption remains 7.22 s per page. NV-Embed is a text embedding reference, not a page encoder Lee et al. (2024). Figure 3(a) summarises relative gains: MUL and MMLong F1 move more than gold DocVQA, as expected when the backbone already reads a single gold page well.

6.5 Failure modes

Three errors recur. First, scanned pages at very low DPI: CAVR tags them as text, EtextE_{\mathrm{text}} still cannot resolve a 6-pt footnote, and WSPS then trusts a visually similar but higher-resolution neighbour. Second, unanswerable (UNA) items where a near-neighbour table looks sufficient; VET prunes polarity conflicts but not “the document never states this KPI.” Third, decks whose evidence is a tiny crop inside a large infographic: late interaction hits the page, CAVR marks mixed, and the chart expert reads the wrong panel. We also do not run an agent that can issue a second retrieval after reading Yang et al. (2026); Zuo et al. (2026b); Sourati et al. (2026); a missed page stays missed. MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 is a smaller phone-side reader we did not swap in Yao et al. (2024a).

7 Conclusion

Visual document RAG fails when retrieved pages are treated as interchangeable in-context shots, when a weak retriever hides the page a strong reader could use, and when cross-page evidence is a flat list. We freeze Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and a ColPali / VisRAG-Ret index, and insert CAVR, WSPS, and VET so pages are routed by skill, reranked by a 7B teacher, and consumed as layout-anchored threads. The same 7B envelope improves gold-page ChartQA and InfoVQA, VisRAG-protocol generation, MMLongBench-Doc retrieve-then-read (especially MUL and financial reports), and ViDoRe TATQ, at 0.33 s extra QA latency. Remaining work is low-DPI scans, unanswerable near-neighbours, and a second-look retrieval step that can still be cancelled when the thread is already sufficient.
